acceptance: 1) Caller/wiring point: real Auth.js Credentials -> authorizeLogin. For an enabled account, totp mode checks only the account and code; password mode checks the current password and code. Unknown mode, totp without enablement, nonempty recoveryCode, and unknown accounts all produce the same generic failure and no device row (E-06, E-96). 2) Atomically consume the current secret/sv/step; at most one sign-in/concurrent request succeeds for one time step. An old-secret code cannot succeed across a racing reset. Preserve all six digits including leading zeros and retain existing rate limits (E-72, E-08). 3) An unenrolled account must complete initial enrollment with the existing one-time token. Real enroll/confirm recheck tokenhash/expiry/sv/pendingSecret in the final transaction; incorrect, expired, and concurrent confirmations do not commit. passwordlessEnabled remains false until confirmation (E-05, E-08).

E-05.scene: C-03 Authenticator enrollment and the passwordless-default toggle
E-05.trigger: The account has not yet enrolled an authenticator.
E-05.expect: Continue through an existing usable sign-in method into enrollment. Enable passwordless-default sign-in only after the new authenticator has been correctly verified; do not enable it for all accounts in bulk.

E-06.scene: C-03 Authenticator enrollment and the passwordless-default toggle
E-06.trigger: The owner of an enrolled account enables the toggle after fresh identity verification.
E-06.expect: Ordinary sign-in requires only an email address or account identifier and an authenticator code. Recovery codes belong to a separate recovery entry point; a password is no longer required for this mode.

E-08.scene: C-03 Authenticator enrollment and the passwordless-default toggle
E-08.trigger: An enrollment code is wrong or expired, a submission is repeated, or switches occur concurrently.
E-08.expect: Test all four triggers separately. In the final transaction, recheck the pending enrollment record, validity period, and current credential version. Do not commit wrong, expired, or replayed submissions; at most one of two concurrent switches succeeds. After a failure, querying the account must still show at least one verified sign-in method. Follow section 09 without inventing another sign-in method.

E-72.scene: Fresh identity verification for sensitive settings
E-72.trigger: The same TOTP time step has already been consumed by sign-in, another sensitive operation, or a concurrent request.
E-72.expect: Atomically consume the account's authenticator time step so later requests cannot issue another ActionGrant. The client may wait for the next code and retry; do not reintroduce recovery codes into ordinary sign-in.

E-96.trigger: mode is unknown, totp mode was not enabled by the account owner, or ordinary Credentials carries a nonempty recoveryCode.
E-96.expect: Test each invalid mode, totp without owner enablement, and a nonempty recoveryCode on ordinary Credentials. They must all produce the same generic Auth.js failure, issue no admin session, and return no account-existence distinction. Valid password/totp requests validate only their respective mode. Test the established rate-limit/error protocol and retain sign-in for valid users.
